meta.title: KanjiFlow — Learn Japanese
meta.description: Learn hiragana, katakana, and kanji with handwriting, audio, and spaced repetition.

ui.subtitle: Kana and kanji, one review at a time.
ui.onboardingDescription: Tell me your name and preferred reminder time to personalize your progress. Then you can take a quick tour or jump straight in.
ui.onboardingLanguageHint: You can change it later from the globe at the top.
ui.onboardingNameRequired: Enter your name to save your profile.
ui.onboardingReadyToast: Profile ready. You can start practicing.
ui.tourSkippedToast: Tour skipped. Explore KanjiFlow at your own pace.
ui.tourGoalText: This bar tracks unique cards reviewed today. You define the goal in Profile and the app marks your daily progress.
ui.tourLessonText: Pick a lesson, script, and session. Recommended avoids unnecessary repeats when better cards are available.
ui.tourBoardText: Draw the character here. It works with mouse, stylus, or finger on touch screens.
ui.tourRevealText: This button shows the answer with the stroke-order guide layered on top so you can compare your drawing.
ui.tourEvaluatorText: Turn it on to compare your stroke with the correct one as you draw: green is accurate, yellow is acceptable, and red is far off. The similarity percentage appears after you press "Show answer".
ui.tourRatingText: After seeing the answer, mark again, hard, good, or easy. That schedules when the card returns.
ui.tourStudyText: In Study you can browse characters without affecting your practice session.
ui.tourSearchText: Search by character, reading, or meaning. You can also filter by kana, kanji, or favorites.
ui.tourCardsText: Open any card to see examples and practice stroke order.
ui.tourProgressMapText: See every character in a color grid: white is pending, red is urgent, green means you're on track, and blue means mastered. Tap any character to practice it, or launch a session focused on your red items.
ui.tourAudioText: The speaker icon plays the character's audio. You'll find it next to the main reading, the example word, the onyomi, the kunyomi, and the example sentence, plus in Practice before and after revealing the answer.
ui.tourAnimationText: This button cycles the animation speed (1x, 2x, 4x). Also notice the small numbers next to each stroke: they mark where it starts and the order it's drawn in.
ui.tourFavoritesText: The star saves a card as a favorite. Later you can filter them in Study and practice them from the Favorites session.
ui.tourExamText: Pick a topic and a number of questions to test yourself with multiple choice on readings and meanings. It's a new beta feature.
ui.tourProfileChipText: This chip shows your name and achievement level. Tap it to open your full profile: goals, stroke evaluator, stats, achievements, and history.
ui.tourProfileGoalText: In Profile you choose how many unique cards you want to review each day. Ten a day is a steady mastery goal.
ui.tourReminderTimeText: Choose the time you prefer to study. When you turn on the bell, KanjiFlow will use this time for the next reminder.
ui.tourStatsText: Here you see active days, goals reached, streaks, and lists of viewed, missed, mastered, and upcoming cards.
ui.reminderOnLabel: Practice reminder is on. Next reminder: {time}.
ui.reminderDueLabel: Reminder is due. Time to practice.
ui.reminderEnabledToast: Reminder is on. I will remind you at the chosen time.
ui.reminderEnabledToastWithNotifications: Reminder is on. I will also use browser notifications if available.
ui.reminderDueToast: It has been 24 h since your last practice. Ready for a review?
ui.progressReady: You are up to date. You can learn new cards.
ui.profileSummary: Today you have reviewed {count} of {goal} unique cards and {reviews} total reviews.
ui.reminderTimeHint: The bell will use this time when reminders are turned on.
ui.strokeEvaluatorToggleLabel: Turn the stroke evaluator on or off
ui.strokeEvaluatorEnabledToast: Stroke evaluator turned on. Your stroke must reach {threshold}% to be graded. For more options, go to your profile.
ui.strokeEvaluatorDisabledToast: Stroke evaluator turned off. Rate yourself manually. For more options, go to your profile.
ui.strokeGateMessage: Similarity {score}% — you need {threshold}%. Remember that stroke order matters for the evaluation too. Clear and try again, or turn off the evaluator with the button next to the canvas.
ui.profileListsDescription: Review what you saw today, what you missed, what you have mastered, and what is coming soon.
ui.emptyViewedToday: You have not reviewed cards today yet.
ui.tourRestartDescription: Want to go over how KanjiFlow works?
ui.progressMapProfileDescription: See at a glance which characters you've mastered, which need review, and which you're missing.
ui.progressMapDescription: Tap any character to practice it. The colors show how you're doing.
ui.progressMapNoRedToast: You have no cards to review in this category right now.
ui.progressMapNoMasteredToast: You haven't mastered any card in this category yet.
ui.dataDescription: Export or import a local copy of your progress, profile, and statistics.
ui.aboutDescription: A daily practice app for learning Japanese one stroke at a time.
ui.updateOnboarding: Brand splash screen, welcome prompt, and first-run tour.
ui.updateAchievements: Achievement levels and visible version on the splash screen.
ui.updateN4: Complete N4 coverage by the JLPT Sensei reference, with 170 N4 kanji, examples, and stroke guides.
ui.updateKanjiAudio: Kanji audio now uses main readings with pauses.
ui.updateStudyFavorites: Direct favorites and a mastered filter in Study.
ui.updateProfileGoals: Profile, daily goal, and per-day statistics.
ui.updateDirectFeedback: Direct recommendation sending to Google Sheets.
ui.updateI18n: Multilingual interface in Spanish, English, German, French, and Portuguese.
ui.kanjivgAttributionText: Stroke order and shape for N5, N4, N3, and N2 kanji use data from the KanjiVG project (Ulrich Apel), licensed under Creative Commons BY-SA 3.0.
ui.animcjkAttributionText: Stroke order and shape for hiragana and katakana use data from the AnimCJK project, licensed under the GNU LGPL.
ui.strokeModelDifferenceNote: Kanji and kana use two different stroke-data models, so the stroke style looks a little different between them — that's normal. With the stroke evaluator turned on, kana uses that model as a background guide; if you turn it off from your profile, kana goes back to showing the more stylized strokes it always had.
ui.feedbackDescription: Write between 10 and 500 characters. It will be saved directly for review.
ui.feedbackPlaceholder: Tell me what you would improve…
ui.feedbackTooShort: Write at least 10 characters before sending.
ui.feedbackTooLong: The comment must be under 500 characters.
ui.feedbackSent: Thank you. Your recommendation was sent.
ui.feedbackSendError: It could not be sent right now. Try again in a moment.
ui.examSetupDescription: Choose a topic and how many questions you want. We'll quiz you at random on meaning and onyomi — never on stroke order.
ui.examNoQuestions: There aren't enough kanji in this topic.
ui.examDisclaimerText: Exam mode is a beta feature and still under development. Do you want to continue?
ui.kanaEvaluatorNoticeTitle: The kana stroke evaluator is still a work in progress
ui.kanaEvaluatorNoticeText: The stroke evaluator for hiragana and katakana uses a different model than kanji and is still under development, so it can mark strokes as wrong even when they're actually fine. The kanji evaluator (KanjiVG) is more accurate. If you'd rather, you can turn it off now or later from your profile.
ui.examFeedbackDescription: Tell us what you thought of this new feature. Write between 10 and 500 characters.
ui.noCardsQuestion: There are no characters with these filters.
ui.noCardsHint: Try another lesson or a different session.
ui.kanjiHint: You can listen to a reading as a hint.
ui.specialHint: Check the lesson description if you need to remember the rule.
ui.kanaHint: Trace the character inside the grid.
ui.practiceCanvasLabel: Board for writing the Japanese character
ui.recognitionIntro: Recognition compares the final shape; it does not evaluate stroke order yet.
ui.ratingLegend: How easy was it to remember?
ui.dueAgain: We will see it again in this session.
ui.emptyResults: No characters were found with those filters.
ui.kunyomiOkuriganaNote: The kanji represents the reading root. The part in parentheses is okurigana, written in hiragana to complete the word.
ui.recognitionLoading: Loading Japanese recognition. The first time can take a while.
ui.recognitionMatched: Recognized as “{detected}”. Check the stroke order with the guide.
ui.recognitionMissedToast: The shape was not recognized. You can self-evaluate.
ui.recognitionError: Recognition could not be used. Practice and self-evaluation are still available.
ui.backupInvalid: The backup could not be imported.
ui.loadErrorQuestion: The content could not be loaded.
ui.loadErrorHint: Open the app from a local server or check datos.csv.

hira-basic-1.title: 1. Hiragana: vowels and K/S

hira-voiced.description: Practice the G, Z, D, B, and P sounds.

kata-voiced.title: 9. Katakana with dakuten
kata-voiced.description: Practice the G, Z, D, B, and P sounds in katakana.
